newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on auction hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down on auction hopes.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed down 100 basis points at 21.50 percent on Tuesday on market liquidity amid forecasts that primary rates were about to fall, traders said.
"Secondary rates are backing a fall in auction rates," a trader said.

A Reuters survey of nine Mexico City money market traders showed they forecast an average assignment rate of 22.20 percent for bellwether 28-day Cetes. This would be a fall of 97 basis points since last week.
"Judging by secondary market levels, primary rates should fall that much. Some dealers are, however, planing low bids at this auction, due to the review of Bonde rates," a trader said.
The central bank is due to announce results for the primary auction at 1830 local time.
Bondes are government securities that pay a premium rate above primary Cetes rates.
Overnight rates on bank paper, meanwhile, closed down 110 basis points at 23.40 percent.
Dealers said a stable peso also boosted market liquidity. Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 3.7 centavos firmer at 7.9310/7.9350 per dollar.

Banco de Mexico offset surplus liquidity in the market by draining 4.655 billion pesos through five secondary auctions, which it assigned at rates of 23.78-24.13 percent, to fall due in one to 23 days. Total liquidity of 2.766 billion pesos was slated to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation. Traders said they nonetheless expected some liquidity pressures from demand for cash ahead of the forthcoming long weekend.
